newsitem.title: MEXICO: Phillips Petroleum enters Mexico partnership.
newsitem.headline: Phillips Petroleum enters Mexico partnership.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum said Tuesday in a paid advertisement that its Phillips Driscopipe unit will join forces with Promotora Mexicana de Industrias to make high density polyethylene tubing in Mexico.

The companies have signed a letter of intent to produce more than 10,000 tonnes of tubing for Mexico and to export to Central America and the northern part of South America beginning in March, the statement said.

"This company will provide the tubing for the important developments expected in our country in natural gas distribution, city water systems and ducts used in fiber-optic communication," said Javier Miguel, representative of Promotora Mexicana de Industrias.
The new company parthership will be called Driscopipe Mexicana, owned 51 percent by Promotora Mexicana de Industrias and 49 percent by Phillips.

Phillips Driscopipe is based in Richardson, Texas, and produces more than 100,000 tonnes annually of polyethylene tubing in five U.S. factories. Promotora Mexicana de Industrias is part of Grupo Miguel, a Mexico City conglomerate that produces plastic, textiles and auto parts.
